findings.explanation: Informal discount slang like 'sasta' or 'loot lo' undermines our curated vintage positioning.

findings.clauseQuote: Informal street slang that detracts from a curated, premium experience is banned, including: "chindi", "kachra", "ghanta", "faltu", "bakwaas", "chapri", "sasta", "loot lo", and "bhasad".
findings.explanation: The caption uses the prohibited slang terms "sasta" and "chindi", which are explicitly listed as banned in TM-007. Such slang undermines the premium, curated brand experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace "sasta and chindi" with approved wording such as "affordable and curated".

findings.clauseQuote: Keep the tone friendly but not too casual. Maintain warmth and wit without devolving into unprofessional slang or careless internet vernacular.
findings.explanation: "Yo bro" is overly casual internet slang and violates BV-007, which requires the tone to stay friendly yet professional without unprofessional vernacular.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace "Yo bro" with a friendlier, on‑brand greeting such as "Hey friends".

findings.clauseQuote: Every post must include exactly one clear, singular call-to-action (CTA) (e.g., "Tap link in bio to shop" or "Visit our Bandra pop-up this Saturday"). Multiple competing CTAs confuse users and dilute engagement.
findings.postQuote: Yo bro, sasta and chindi collections are out, curated vintage is in! Happy Festivities from Thrift-It. #ThriftIt
findings.explanation: The caption contains no call‑to‑action, breaching SR-002 which mandates exactly one clear CTA in every post.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single CTA, e.g., "Tap link in bio to shop now!" at the end of the caption.
